title: Hospital Ka 1 ICU Bed Roz Kitna Kamata Hai?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. 'Per unit per day' reels like the sleeper bus trip and the PS5 hour let viewers calculate along. Owning a hospital is a prestige dream for doctors and investors, and ARPOB is a public number listed hospital chains publish every quarter. The reel can contrast the glamorous image with slow payback.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: HOSPITAL ECONOMICS (ARPOB, occupancy, cost per bed, 50-bed break-even)
Prepared 3 Nov 2026. Figures are from the latest results I could find. Estimate-type figures are labelled.

**HEADLINE CAVEATS FOR THE SCRIPTWRITER**
- Listed chains (Apollo, Max, Fortis) publish hard numbers. No public database exists for 50-bed nursing homes.
- Every small-hospital figure below comes from consultants, project-report vendors or broker notes. Label these "estimates" on screen.
- Sources disagree on break-even time and cost per bed. I show the ranges instead of picking one.

**1. ARPOB: WHAT ONE OCCUPIED BED EARNS**
- Definition: ARPOB is revenue per occupied bed per day. It acts as a proxy for price power, case complexity and patient mix. [https://kenthospitals.com/uncategorized/indian-hospital-efficiency-metrics-arpob-occupancy/]
- Max Healthcare, Q2 FY26 (latest Max ARPOB I found): ₹77.3 thousand per day, vs ₹76.2 thousand in Q2 FY25. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/capital-market-news/max-healthcare-clocks-59-yoy-jump-in-q2-pat-125111500547_1.html]
- Max Q2 FY27 reports revenue per patient instead: ₹2.31 lakh, up 8% from ₹2.14 lakh. [https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/max-healthcare-reports-10-pat-jump-to-448-crore-in-q2-with-revenue-climbing-20-to-3219-crore-capacity-expanding]
- Fortis, Q1 FY27: ARPOB improved to ₹2.71 crore a year, from ₹2.64 crore a year earlier. [https://www.indianpharmapost.com/hospitals/fortis-healthcare-reports-18-revenue-growth-to-rs-2545-crore-in-q1-fy27-21277]
- Fortis daily ARPOB (period not stated in the article, reported Dec 2025): up 9% year-on-year to ₹66,301. Apollo reported ₹60,588. [https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/healthcarebiotech/Indias-Top-Hospitals-See-Stunning-Revenue-Jump-Heres-Why-High-Tech-Treatments-and-Insurance-Are-Driving-Growth/694b9291e10c98d0787ac432]
- Apollo reports revenue per inpatient, not daily ARPOB, in its latest quarter. Average revenue per patient rose 8% year-on-year to ₹1,86,630. [https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy27-earnings-call.pdf]
- Industry range: ARPOB for major chains runs from about ₹38,000 to over ₹74,000 per bed per day. [https://www.brickworkratings.com/Research/Private%20Hospitals%20report_10Nov2025.pdf]
- FY24 ICRA table: Apollo ₹57,488, Aster India ₹40,100, Fortis ₹60,887, Max ₹76,000 per bed per day. [https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/top-indian-private-hospital-chains-announce-major-expansion-in-fy25-124060300894_1.html]
- Small-town benchmark (Yatharth Hospitals, listed, Tier-2/3 North India): group ARPOB reached ₹35,948 in Q2 FY27, up 11% year-on-year. [https://www.investywise.com/yatharth-hospital-trauma-care-services-ltd-strong-q2-fy27-results-strategic-partnership]
- Doctor-owned small hospital (consultant estimate): Tier-II small multi-specialty ARPOB of ₹8,000–12,000 a day, with 55–65% target occupancy. [https://www.actisshealthcare.com/hospital-roi-doctor-owned-hospitals-india]
- Insider fact: ARPOB can rise even if the total bill stays the same. If patients have complex procedures but leave sooner, the daily figure goes up (DAM Capital analyst). [https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/healthcarebiotech/Indias-Top-Hospitals-See-Stunning-Revenue-Jump-Heres-Why-High-Tech-Treatments-and-Insurance-Are-Driving-Growth/694b9291e10c98d0787ac432]
- Insider fact: Hospitals typically earn most of their revenue in the first 1–2 days of admission, through diagnostics, procedures and intensive treatment. [https://devanshmaheshwari.com/hospital-industry-analysis/]
- Another source lists ALOS (average length of stay) as 3.14 days at Apollo in Q1 FY26. [https://finshots.in/archive/what-makes-a-hospital-profitable/]

**2. OCCUPANCY**
- Max, Q2 FY27: average occupancy held steady at 77% despite the large capacity addition. Delhi ran at 79% across 2,676 operational beds. [https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/max-healthcare-q2-fy27-slides-20-revenue-growth-amid-expansion-push-93CH-5673744]
- Apollo, Q1 FY27: occupancy reached 70% overall and 72% at established units. [https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/apollo-hospitals-q1-fy27-slides-margins-expand-digital-losses-narrow-93CH-4857308]
- Fortis, Q2 FY25 (latest occupancy figure I found): 72%. [https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/fortis-healthcare-rises-as-q2-pat-climbs-5-yoy-to-rs-193-cr-124111100335_1.html]
- Industry: occupancy of 61–63% was projected for FY25, with operating margins of 22–23% (Brickwork). [https://www.brickworkratings.com/Research/Private%20Hospitals%20report_10Nov2025.pdf]
- Weak-occupancy example: Yatharth's 300-bed Model Town hospital in Delhi ran at 0–32% occupancy in Q1 with a 90% cash mix. [https://www.tijorifinance.com/company/yatharth-hospital-trauma-care-services-ltd/]

**3. WHAT THE LISTED CHAINS KEEP (EBITDA)**
- Apollo healthcare services, Q1 FY27: EBITDA of ₹8,617 million, a 24.2% margin. [https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/apollo-hospitals-q1-fy27-slides-margins-expand-digital-losses-narrow-93CH-4857308]
- Narayana India hospitals, Q2 FY27: EBITDA margin of 26.8%. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/narayana-health-india-hospital-margin-ppt-cmvyzdisl003b2cpcrfqwr6xw]
- Max: EBITDA per bed was ₹73.4 lakh in Q2 FY26, vs ₹71.2 lakh in Q2 FY25. The source doesn't say whether this is annualised. Check Max's investor deck before using it. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/capital-market-news/max-healthcare-clocks-59-yoy-jump-in-q2-pat-125111500547_1.html]
- Fortis: it expects to improve operating EBITDA margins gradually to the mid-twenties. [https://www.indianpharmapost.com/hospitals/fortis-healthcare-reports-18-revenue-growth-to-rs-2545-crore-in-q1-fy27-21277]
- Industry: operating profit margin was 20.3% in FY24.
